uncited: **Perspective Projection:** Project the single input panorama $I_{\text{rgb}}$ into $K$ perspective images $\{\bar{I}_{\text{rgb}}^k\}$ using different viewing directions.
**Deformable Alignment:** Align the perspective depth maps $\{\bar{I}_d^k\}$ to a canonical learnable panorama depth map $I_d$ by optimizing an alignment objective.
**NeRF Training:** Train the single-view NeRF using the RGB panorama $I_{\text{rgb}}$ and the aligned canonical depth map $I_d$.
* **Scale Ambiguity:** Monocular depth estimation suffers from scale ambiguity, leading to inconsistent depth values in overlapping regions of perspective views.
* **Panorama Warping:** Standard monocular depth estimators fail on 360-degree panoramas warped into rectangular matrices.
* **Visible Regions Only:** The trained NeRF $f_{\text{nerf}}$ only works for visible regions of the single panorama.
* **Time Complexity:** The method involves an initial alignment optimization step over $K$ views and the full NeRF training loop.
* **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing $K$ perspective depth maps and the canonical panorama depth map.
It addresses the limitation of previous single-view NeRF methods that did not fully address geometry consistency.
